prerequisites: Basic notions of electricity, electronics, mathematics, and physics.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.
Introductory knowledge of the different techniques for implementing an automatic control system.
Introductory knowledge of the different tools for modeling, simulation, analysis, and design of automation and control systems.
That the student understands the disciplines involved and integrated into an automation system.

syllabus_topics: Part I: Introduction to automatic regulation. Topic 01.- Introduction to feedback control systems. 1.1. Basic concepts and terminology. 1.2. Introduction to system modeling through physical principles. 1.3. Linearization and normalization. 1.4. Transfer functions of generic industrial elements and systems. 1.5. Laplace transforms. 1.6. Transfer function. 1.7. Graphical representation of control systems: block diagrams.

Part I: Introduction to automatic regulation. Topic 02.- Complete response of control systems. 2.1. First-order systems. 2.2. Second-order systems. 2.3. System identification. 2.4. Higher-order systems: dominant poles.

Part I: Introduction to automatic regulation. Topic 03.- Stability analysis and introduction to control system design. 3.1. Stability: Lyapunov analysis and Routh criterion. 3.2. Technical control specifications. 3.3. Transient response analysis: root locus. 3.4. Steady-state response analysis. 3.5. General considerations for design. 3.6. Design of controllers by dynamic compensation.
Part I: Introduction to automatic regulation. Topic 04.- Frequency response analysis. 4.1. Bode diagrams. 4.2. Series compensation by phase lag. 4.3. Series compensation by phase lead.

Part II: Introduction to automation. Topic 01.- Introduction to logical systems used in automation. 1.1. Concept of digital system. 1.2. Binary numbering system. 1.3. Fundamentals of digital systems: Boolean algebra. 1.4. Logical functions and gates. 1.5. Concept of flip-flop. 1.6. Simplification of logical functions: Karnaugh map method.

Part II: Introduction to automation. Topic 02.- Programmable logic controllers. 2.1. Introduction and types. 2.2. Internal structure and operation. 2.3. Types of inputs and outputs. Wiring. 2.4. Peripherals.

Part II: Introduction to automation. Topic 03.- Programming programmable logic controllers. 3.1. Ladder diagram. 3.2. Basic instructions: SR flip-flop, timer and counter. 3.3. Programming methodology. 3.4. Introduction to state machine. 3.5. Applications with Zelio Soft 2.
assessment_rules: Individual laboratory practices are evaluated based on the adequacy of responses, writing, figures, tables, and comprehension of the problem. Active participation in sessions is necessary for the maximum weighting of each practice. The final exam is a written test, including problem-solving and theoretical-practical questions. Lab attendance is optional and cumulative for weighting, but active participation must be demonstrated. The overall grade is 20% from laboratory practices and 80% from the final written exam.
